description.narrative: Between 20142018 the EU funded and external monitoring team to assess 30 schools with Syrian students to assess CRF indicator 2b. With MoE, the criteria for selection of schools was formulated, monitoring framework, evaluation instruments and indicators were prepared, monitoring visits undertaken and data collected and analysed, culminating in a comprehensive database. In 2018, as a result of sector policy dialogue, quality monitoring was extended to 100 schools, focus shifted from Syrians to all students. This process was the foundation to quality assessment in the education strategic plan, ESP.The calculation of the QPS is based on a monitoring framework, which includes three performance standards (with the related descriptors) which allow for objective judgements on schools performance. Against the descriptors, schools are assessed by the EQAU on a fourpoint scale from 1 (best performing school) to 4 (lowest performing school). These point values are then used to categorise schools into three bands (A) Good; (B) Adequate; (C) In need of improvement. The complex set of qualitative data is then translated into QPS, which provide details for every Performance Standard, broken down into SubDomains. The average(B) is within the range of 2.512.75, these are the schools with satisfactory performance.Band A is QPS within 1.02.25 and Band C is QPS within 2.7514,0.This methodology was praised by the Court of Auditors in a report on data and M&E (2019).
